draft.title: Cortisol
card: Cortisol is a hormone released by the adrenal glands when the body faces a stressor. It is often called a stress hormone.
Cortisol acts more slowly than adrenaline and its effects last longer. It helps keep energy available, by raising blood glucose, while a stressor continues.
In the short term, this helps the body cope with a demand. If cortisol stays high for a long time, it weakens the immune system.
A weaker immune system means the body is less able to fight infection, so a person under long stress may get sick more often.
draft.remember: Cortisol helps the body cope over time, but long-term high levels weaken the immune system.

a.q: What is the main role of cortisol during a stressor that lasts for hours or days?
opts: Keeping energy available while the stressor continues
Giving a brief burst of energy that fades within seconds
Strengthening the immune system as the stressor continues
Slowing the body down so that it can rest and recover
a.why: Cortisol acts slowly and lasts, so it keeps energy available while a stressor continues. It does not strengthen the immune system: if levels stay high for long, it weakens it.
a.clue: Think about what the body needs over a long stressor, not a few seconds.

b.q: Priya has studied under heavy pressure for many weeks and has caught several colds. Which explanation fits the card best?
opts: Long-term high cortisol has weakened her immune system
Cortisol has run out, so she has no energy to fight germs
Cortisol has raised her immune response too much
Her cortisol rose briefly, which always causes illness
b.why: Weeks of stress can keep cortisol high, and long-term high cortisol weakens the immune system, so she is less able to fight infection. A brief rise in cortisol is not the cause, because it helps the body cope in the short term.
b.clue: Ask what happens to the immune system when cortisol stays high for a long time.

a.best: Keeping energy available while the stressor continues

b.best: Long-term high cortisol has weakened her immune system

problems.detail: The distractor 'Her cortisol rose briefly, which always causes illness' uses 'always'. The absolute marks it as wrong to a test-wise student, and it clashes with the card's 'may get sick more often'.
